message.content: Work GitHub issue #68 in this repo using the /hq-work workflow (read AGENTS.md and .agents/skills/hq-work/SKILL.md). Claim with `./hq claim 68 --agent claude`, build strictly inside the issue's Scope, run `./hq check`, rebase on origin/main, open the PR with `./hq pr 68 --body-file .context/pr-68.md` (add --allow-dirty only for untracked generated files you deliberately did not commit; retry once if the push is rejected with commit_refs_rules), then stop and report PR number and evidence. Do not ship/merge. Run `bun install` in the worktree first. Run the anti-slop skill on changed UI. Device-only steps are left for a human. Never read .env files. A local test `speak > names a missing api key from a fresh process` may fail only because of a git-ignored .env.local; say so rather than working around it.

1	---
2	name: hq-work
3	description: 'Use when a human assigns you a GitHub issue ("work on #N" or "/hq-work N"). Takes it from claim to a reviewed PR.'
4	---
5	
6	# hq-work
7	
8	`N` = issue, `<you>` = `claude`, `codex` or `cursor`, `<PR>` = PR number. Windows: `hq.cmd` for `./hq`.
9	
10	1. Claim: `./hq claim N --agent <you>`. If it refuses, stop and tell the human why. Read what it
11	   prints: the issue, work in flight, overlapping files.
12	2. Context before code. Read only the docs the issue needs, then run
13	   `entire search "<topic>"`, `entire graph query "<task>"` and `entire brain brief "<task>"`.
14	   Before rewriting code you did not write: `entire why <file>:<line>`.
15	3. Plan inline in a few bullets. No spec or plan documents.
16	4. Build inside Scope, never in "Do not touch". Small commits, staged by name:
17	   `git add <file> <file> && git commit -m "<what the product can now do>"`.
18	   Push whenever you like: `git push -u origin HEAD`.
19	5. Verify: run the issue's Verify steps, then `./hq check` until it passes.
20	6. Sync with main. Not pushed yet: `git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main`. Already pushed:
21	   `git fetch origin && git merge origin/main` (never force-push). Fix conflicts in your own
22	   changes, `git add <files>`, then `git rebase --continue` or `git commit`. Re-run `./hq check`.
23	7. Write `.context/pr-N.md` (template below; `mkdir -p .context` if needed), then
24	   `./hq pr N --body-file .context/pr-N.md`. It pushes, opens the PR with `Closes #N` and sets
25	   `status:review`. Get the number: `gh pr view --json number,url`.
26	8. Trail: Entire opens a trail for your PR by itself. Check it with `entire trail show`, then run `entire trail ci-pr` (safe to re-run). Only if `trail show` finds none: `entire trail create --title "<issue title> (#N)" --type feature`.
27	9. Review, unless the issue is `size:S`: `entire review`. Fix real findings, commit, `git push`,
28	   re-run `./hq check`. Then `gh pr edit <PR> --add-label review:pass` and `entire trail ready`.
29	10. Report the PR link, check result and risks, then stop. Merge only on "ship it" (`/hq-ship`).
30	
31	PR body template for `.context/pr-N.md`:
32	
33	````markdown
34	## What changed
35	- <what the product can now do>
36	
37	## How verified
38	- <Verify steps you ran and what you saw>
39	```
40	<tail of ./hq check>
41	```
42	
43	## Risks
44	- <what could break, or "none">
45	
46	## Screenshots
47	<UI changes only, else "n/a">
48	````
49	
50	Out of scope: do not do it. Write `.context/new-issue.md` with the headings `### Goal`,
51	`### Acceptance criteria`, `### Scope`, `### Do not touch`, `### Blocked by`, `### Verify`,
52	`### Notes` (say "Found while working on #N" in Notes), then
53	`gh issue create --title "<title>" --body-file .context/new-issue.md --label status:needs-human`.
54	Link it on your issue: `gh issue comment N --body "Follow-up: #M"`. Carry on with your own scope.
55	
56	Stuck (unclear criteria, waiting on another issue, a conflict in code you did not write):
57	`./hq release N --needs-human --note "<one crisp question>"`, then stop.
58	
59	Done means: every acceptance criterion met, `./hq check` passes with its tail in the PR, PR open
60	with evidence, `review:pass` (unless `size:S`).
61

### Goal

Works near you are visible, with their dates and whether they run at night.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Export a selectable `WorksLayer` through `apps/mobile/src/features/works/index.ts` for the city and Quiet Stays maps.
- [ ] Draw stored permit line or polygon geometry when available; use a representative point only as a disclosed approximate location.
- [ ] Selected works show permit source, proposed/actual dates when known, scheduled night-work state and an explicit unknown-schedule state.
- [ ] Distinguish scheduled night work from an observed construction sound outside the council's recommended hours; do not add building or demolition sites to the Street Manager layer.
- [ ] Web and iOS render equivalent overlays, and the layer accepts selected permit refs so Quiet Stays can highlight works behind a score.

### Scope

- `apps/mobile/src/features/works/`

### Do not touch

Other features' folders. Registries: `apps/server/src/trpc/router.ts`, `apps/server/src/main.api.ts`, `apps/server/src/main.worker.ts`, `apps/mobile/app/`. Shared code: `apps/mobile/src/lib/`, `apps/mobile/modules/`, `apps/server/src/integrations/`, `apps/server/src/db/` (adding a new migration file is fine), `packages/shared/src/domain/`, `env.ts`, `.env.example`, root config.

### Blocked by

#66, #12, #113, #111, #114

### Verify

- `./hq check`
- `cd apps/mobile && bunx expo export --platform web` succeeds
- Run the `anti-slop` skill on every changed screen and component

### Notes

- Cloud agents: yes.
- Parallel safety: stay inside Scope. Shared code changes go through their own `platform` issue (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, Rules that keep parallel agents apart).

content.thinking:
I'm settling on the fixed ink color for the lines and polygons. Since the map library has no way to take child layers, I'll make WorksLayer a self-contained component that renders its own MapView with the works features and a details card, driven by center, radius, date range, selected permit refs, style, and an onSelect callback. I'm also considering an optional works prop so it can be tested directly.

I'm checking how useAccount handles the tRPC calls and how the map treats color. MapView only takes one selectedId, so highlighting several permits at once won't work through it. My plan is to add a marker at each highlighted work's representative point, with an accent color and an id like `highlight:<ref>`, and to flag point-precision locations as approximate in the card. I'm also considering a small pure `describeWork` helper for the night-work states, with a note that scheduled night work comes from the permit and is not an observed sound.
